body.statement: For constants whose bounds contain the displayed Jacobian ranges and for \(\beta\) below the displayed displacement and cut-locus margins, the construction in def:separable-witness satisfies \(P^{\mathrm{sep}}\in\mathcal F_s\). The translation coordinates in the three triples returned by \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}\) are zero; the potential coordinates for \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}\) are respectively \(-0.1\cos(2\pi u_1)/(2\pi^2)\) and \(-0.15\cos(2\pi u_1)/(2\pi^2)+0.05\cos(2\pi u_2)/(2\pi^2)\). At \(u=(1/4,1/4)\) and \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\), its translation-aware displacement is \(\operatorname{Disp}_{\mathbb T}(T,y)=(0.05/\pi,-0.05/\pi)\neq0\), its outer Jacobian is positive definite, and equal cell sizes give \(V_j=I_2/\pi\).
body.justification: The witness proves nonemptiness with a nonzero causal arrow and avoids relying only on the identity-map law.
body.gap: The available uniform-law calculation has zero displacement; this witness keeps the critical constant while producing a genuine bivariate effect.
body.consumer: The witness supplies the first reproducible analytic benchmark for the proposed nonseparable numerical kill test and for software validation.
